claim: Chondrocytes in the resting zone of the postnatal growth plate are characterized by slow cell cycle progression.
source: Chondrocytes in the resting zone of the postnatal growth plate are characterized by slow cell cycle progression, and encompass a population of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP)-expressing skeletal stem cells that contribute to the formation of columnar chondrocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of resting zone chondrocytes.

claim: The resting zone encompasses a population of PTHrP-expressing skeletal stem cells that contribute to the formation of columnar chondrocytes.
source: Chondrocytes in the resting zone of the postnatal growth plate are characterized by slow cell cycle progression, and encompass a population of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP)-expressing skeletal stem cells that contribute to the formation of columnar chondrocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of the resting zone.

claim: A genetic pulse-chase approach using a chondrocyte-specific doxycycline-controllable Tet-Off system can isolate slow cycling, label-retaining chondrocytes (LRCs).
source: We undertook a genetic pulse-chase approach to isolate slow cycling, label-retaining chondrocytes (LRCs) using a chondrocyte-specific doxycycline-controllable Tet-Off system regulating expression of histone 2B-linked GFP.
evidence: This is a methodological claim describing the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Comparative RNA-seq analysis identified significant enrichment of inhibitors and activators for Wnt signaling in LRCs and non-LRCs, respectively.
source: Comparative RNA-seq analysis identified significant enrichment of inhibitors and activators for Wnt signaling in LRCs and non-LRCs, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the RNA-seq analysis presented in the study.

claim: Activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes using Pthlh-creER and Apc-floxed allele impaired their ability to form columnar chondrocytes.
source: Activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes using Pthlh-creER and Apc-floxed allele impaired their ability to form columnar chondrocytes.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the functional validation experiments.

claim: Slow-cycling chondrocytes are maintained in a Wnt-inhibitory environment within the resting zone.
source: Therefore, slow-cycling chondrocytes are maintained in a Wnt-inhibitory environment within the resting zone, unraveling a novel mechanism regulating maintenance and differentiation of PTHrP+ skeletal stem cells of the postnatal growth plate.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on the RNA-seq and functional validation data.

claim: The epiphyseal growth plate is an innovation of amniotes (reptiles, birds and mammals) that facilitates explosive endochondral bone growth.
source: The epiphyseal growth plate, a disk of cartilaginous tissues with characteristic columns of chondrocytes formed between the primary and secondary ossification centers, is an innovation of amniotes (reptiles, birds and mammals) that facilitates explosive endochondral bone growth (Wuelling and Vortkamp, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wuelling and Vortkamp, 2019.

claim: The postnatal growth plate is composed of three morphologically distinct layers of resting, proliferating and hypertrophic zones.
source: The postnatal growth plate is composed of three morphologically distinct layers of resting, proliferating and hypertrophic zones, in which chondrocytes continue to proliferate well into adulthood, especially in mice, therefore functioning as the engine for endochondral bone growth (Hallett et al., 2019; Kronenberg, 2003).
evidence: This is a well-established anatomical description supported by citations.

claim: Chondrocytes continue to proliferate well into adulthood, especially in mice, functioning as the engine for endochondral bone growth.
source: The postnatal growth plate is composed of three morphologically distinct layers of resting, proliferating and hypertrophic zones, in which chondrocytes continue to proliferate well into adulthood, especially in mice, therefore functioning as the engine for endochondral bone growth (Hallett et al., 2019; Kronenberg, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hallett et al., 2019 and Kronenberg, 2003.

claim: By adulthood, a large majority of hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo apoptosis or transdifferentiate into osteoblasts.
source: By adulthood, a large majority of hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo apoptosis or transdifferentiate into osteoblasts, marking the completion of the longitudinal growth phase and skeletal maturation (Zhou et al., 2014; Park et al., 2015; Hallett et al., 2021; Roach et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2014a; Yang et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Early studies postulated that resting chondrocytes feed their daughter cells into the adjacent proliferating zone and contribute to longitudinal growth of postnatal endochondral bones.
source: First, early studies postulated that resting chondrocytes feed their daughter cells into the adjacent proliferating zone and contribute to longitudinal growth of postnatal endochondral bones (Hunziker, 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hunziker, 1994.

claim: The resting zone has been established as a niche for skeletal stem cells, initially demonstrated by surgical auto-transplantation experiments in rabbits.
source: More recently, the resting zone has been established as a niche for skeletal stem cells, initially demonstrated by surgical auto-transplantation experiments in rabbits (Abad et al., 2002), and subsequently by lineage-tracing experiments in mice (Mizuhashi et al., 2018; Newton et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Abad et al., 2002, Mizuhashi et al., 2018, and Newton et al., 2019.

claim: Chondrocytes in the resting zone express PTHrP that maintains proliferation of chondrocytes in a cell non-autonomous manner and delays their hypertrophic differentiation.
source: Second, chondrocytes in the resting zone express parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) that maintains proliferation of chondrocytes in a cell non-autonomous manner and delays their hypertrophic differentiation, thus sustaining longitudinal growth (Schipani et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Schipani et al., 1997.

claim: The proliferating zone is concertedly maintained by PTHrP released from the resting zone and Indian hedgehog (Ihh) synthesized by pre-hypertrophic chondrocytes.
source: The proliferating zone is concertedly maintained by PTHrP released from the resting zone and Indian hedgehog (Ihh) synthesized by pre-hypertrophic chondrocytes; the proliferating zone in turn provides instructive cues to regulate cell fates of PTHrP+ chondrocytes (Mizuhashi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mizuhashi et al., 2018.

claim: G protein stimulatory subunit-α (Gsα) and Gq/G11α G proteins, which are coupled with the PTH/PTHrP receptor (PPR), are both required for maintaining quiescent stem-like chondrocytes.
source: G protein stimulatory subunit-α (Gsα), Gq/G11α G proteins, which are coupled with the PTH/PTHrP receptor (PPR), are both required for maintaining quiescent stem-like chondrocytes (Chagin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chagin et al., 2014.

claim: Pan-chondrocyte ablation of Gsα causes premature differentiation of stem-like resting chondrocytes into the proliferative pool, resulting in accelerated endochondral bone growth.
source: Pan-chondrocyte ablation of Gsα (Col2a1-creER; Gnasf/f) causes premature differentiation of stem-like resting chondrocytes into the proliferative pool, resulting in accelerated endochondral bone growth.
evidence: This is a finding from previous research cited in the introduction.

claim: Combined inactivation of Gq/G11α and Gsα causes a more severe phenotype associated with growth plate fusion.
source: Further, combined inactivation of Gq/G11α through a mutant PPR (Guo et al., 2002) and Gsα (Col2a1-creER, Gnasf/f; PPRD/D [Pth1rtm4Hmk]) causes a more severe phenotype associated with growth plate fusion.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Guo et al., 2002.

claim: PPR-mediated Gsα and Gq/G11α synergistically maintain quiescence of resting chondrocytes and their differentiation into columnar chondrocytes.
source: Therefore, PPR-mediated Gsα and Gq/G11α synergistically maintain quiescence of resting chondrocytes and their differentiation into columnar chondrocytes (Chagin et al., 2014); however, whether this regulation occurs cell-autonomously in resting chondrocytes has not been determined.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chagin et al., 2014.

claim: Non-canonical Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling plays a key role in facilitating asymmetric divisions of resting chondrocytes.
source: Non-canonical Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling plays a key role in facilitating asymmetric divisions of resting chondrocytes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Oriented division, rearrangement and intercalation of chondrocyte clones in the resting zone, and their subsequent asymmetric divisions into their daughter cells aligned with the axis of growth are the hallmark characteristic of growth plate chondrocytes.
source: Oriented division, rearrangement and intercalation of chondrocyte clones in the resting zone, and their subsequent asymmetric divisions into their daughter cells aligned with the axis of growth are the hallmark characteristic of growth plate chondrocytes (Li et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2017a.

claim: Misregulation of non-canonical Wnt/PCP signaling via dominant-negative forms of Frizzled receptors results in severe shortening of the growth plate.
source: In fact, misregulation of non-canonical Wnt/PCP signaling via dominant-negative forms of Frizzled receptors results in severe shortening of the growth plate (Hartmann and Tabin, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hartmann and Tabin, 2000.

claim: Oriented cell division is sensitive to both high and low PCP activity mediated in part by Fzd7.
source: Oriented cell division is sensitive to both high and low PCP activity mediated in part by Fzd7 (Li and Dudley, 2009; Li et al., 2017b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li and Dudley, 2009 and Li et al., 2017b.

claim: Wnt5a signals to establish PCP in chondrocytes along the proximal-distal axis through regulation of Vangl2.
source: In addition, Wnt5a signals to establish PCP in chondrocytes along the proximal-distal axis through regulation of Vangl2 (Gao et al., 2011; Randall et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gao et al., 2011 and Randall et al., 2012.

claim: Col2a1-tTA transgenic mice were generated by pronuclear injection of a NotI-digested 8.4 kb gene construct into B6SJLF1 fertilized eggs.
source: Col2a1-tTA transgenic mice were generated by pronuclear injection of a NotI-digested 8.4 kb gene construct containing a 3 kb mouse Col2a1 promoter and a 3 kb fragment of intron one ligated to a splice acceptor sequence followed by an internal ribosome-entry site (IRES) (Ovchinnikov et al., 2000), tetracycline-controlled transactivator (tTA) and the SV40 large T antigen polyadenylation signal (Takara Bio, Mountain View, CA), into B6SJLF1 fertilized eggs.
evidence: This is a methodological description of how the transgenic mice were generated.

claim: The Col2a1-tTA transgene was inserted 16kbp downstream of Pellino2 on Chromosome 14.
source: The insertion site of the Col2a1-tTA transgene was determined based on the Genome Walker Universal system (Takara Bio). The Col2a1-tTA transgene was inserted 16kbp downstream of Pellino2 on Chromosome 14.
evidence: This is a specific finding about the transgene insertion site.

claim: Most chondrocytes in the growth plate were marked by a high level of H2B-EGFP at P7 in double heterozygous Col2a1-tTA/+; TRE-H2B-EGFP/+ mice.
source: While most of chondrocytes in the growth plate were marked by a high level of H2B-EGFP at P7 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b), fewer than half of columnar chondrocytes in the growth plate were marked by H2B-EGFP at P21 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c), demonstrating the inefficiency of the Tet system in postnatal growth plate chondrocytes.
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Fewer than half of columnar chondrocytes in the growth plate were marked by H2B-EGFP at P21 in double heterozygous Col2a1-tTA/+; TRE-H2B-EGFP/+ mice, demonstrating the inefficiency of the Tet system in postnatal growth plate chondrocytes.
source: While most of chondrocytes in the growth plate were marked by a high level of H2B-EGFP at P7 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b), fewer than half of columnar chondrocytes in the growth plate were marked by H2B-EGFP at P21 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c), demonstrating the inefficiency of the Tet system in postnatal growth plate chondrocytes.
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 1—figure supplement 1c and represents an interpretation of the data.

claim: A great fraction of columnar chondrocytes was marked by H2B-EGFP in double homozygous Col2a1-tTA/Col2a1-tTA; TRE-H2B-EGFP/TRE-H2B-EGFP mice at P21.
source: To circumvent this problem, we further generated double homozygous Col2a1-tTA/Col2a1-tTA; TRE-H2B-EGFP/TRE-H2B-EGFP mice and analyzed these mice at P21 without doxycycline. A great fraction of columnar chondrocytes was marked by H2B-EGFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d), indicating that the labeling efficiency can be improved in a transgene dosage-dependent manner in this system.
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 1—figure supplement 1d.

claim: The labeling efficiency can be improved in a transgene dosage-dependent manner in the Col2a1-tTA; TRE-H2B-EGFP system.
source: A great fraction of columnar chondrocytes was marked by H2B-EGFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d), indicating that the labeling efficiency can be improved in a transgene dosage-dependent manner in this system.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing heterozygous and homozygous mice.

claim: After 5 weeks of chase, the H2B-EGFP signal was largely abrogated in the growth plate region, with only a small fraction of cells in the resting zone near the top of the growth plate retaining H2B-EGFP.
source: We fed double heterozygous Col2a1-tTA/+; TRE-H2B-EGFP/+ mice with doxycycline for 5 weeks starting from P21 to shut off de novo H2B-EGFP expression. We started the chase at P21 because the secondary ossification center was fully developed within the epiphysis by this time. After the chase, the H2B-EGFP signal was largely abrogated in the growth plate region, with only a small fraction of cells in the resting zone near the top of the growth plate retaining H2B-EGFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e, arrowheads).
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 1—figure supplement 1e.

claim: A low level of H2B-EGFP signal persisted in adjacent osteoblasts and osteocytes in the epiphysis even after the chase.
source: However, we also noticed that a low level of H2B-EGFP signal persisted in adjacent osteoblasts and osteocytes in the epiphysis even after the chase (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e, arrows), making it difficult to distinguish LRCs from these cells.
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 1—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Osteoblasts and osteocytes expressed a low level of H2B-EGFP in TRE-H2B-EGFP/+ mice without a Col2a1-tTA transgene at P28.
source: Analysis of TRE-H2B-EGFP/+ mice without a Col2a1-tTA transgene at P28 revealed that osteoblasts and osteocytes expressed a low level of H2B-EGFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f, arrows).
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 1—figure supplement 1f.

claim: LRCs can be identified within the top of the growth plate by a chondrocyte-specific Tet-Off system regulating H2B-EGFP expression.
source: These findings indicate that LRCs can be identified within the top of the growth plate by a chondrocyte-specific Tet-Off system regulating H2B-EGFP expression, although these cells cannot be easily distinguished from adjacent osteoblasts and osteocytes solely based on fluorescent intensity in histological sections.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The cells in the proliferating zone had weaker H2B-EGFP signal than those of the resting zone after two weeks of chase at P35.
source: The quantification of CTCF values through the entire column revealed that the cells in the proliferating zone (PZ) had weaker H2B-EGFP signal than those of the resting zone (RZ), and the cells in the pre-hypertrophic (PHZ) and hypertrophic zones (HZ) had yet weaker H2B-EGFP signal (Figure 1b, center panel, yellow numbers, Figure 1b; Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on quantification shown in Figure 1b.

claim: H2B-EGFP CTCF values decreased significantly upon one cell division.
source: The side-by-side comparison of CTCF values between EdU+ cells in the proliferating zone and their preceding EdU-negative cells in the resting zone further revealed that H2B-EGFP CTCF values decreased significantly upon one cell division (Figure 1c, Figure 1—source data 2, P35: H2B-EGFP CTCF, EdU- cells in RZ = 267,184.6±109,457.8; EdU+ cells in PZ = 131,892.0±83,344.8, n=four mice, 24 cell-pairs [p<0.0001]).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data shown in Figure 1c with statistical significance.

claim: The average fold change between EdU-negative and EdU-positive cells was 2.03, suggesting that H2B-EGFP intensity decreases by a factor of two following one cell division.
source: The average fold change between EdU-negative and EdU-positive cells was 2.03, suggesting that H2B-EGFP intensity decreases by a factor of two following one cell division (Figure 1b,c), as expected from the fact that histone-bound GFP is distributed equally between the two daughter cells upon cell division.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis with a mechanistic interpretation.

claim: The cells with the top 10% brightness were localized to the resting zone at the top of the growth plate.
source: Further, the cells with the top 10% brightness were localized to RZ at the top of the growth plate; while there were 27 cells in this given column of chondrocytes, the three brightest cells (374,012; 343,652; 264,697) were localized to RZ (Figure 1b, center panel, arrowheads).
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 1b.

claim: Based on quantitative histological data, cells with the top 10% brightness were designated as LRCs.
source: Thus, based on these quantitative histological data, we designated the cells with the top 10% brightness as LRCs.
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on the quantitative data.

claim: A great majority of cells in the epiphysis, including those in the growth plate and the secondary ossification center, but not as many on the articular surface, were H2B-EGFPhigh at P21 without doxycycline in Col2-Q mice.
source: First, we analyzed Col2-Q mice at P21 without doxycycline ('No Chase'). A great majority of cells in the epiphysis, including those in the growth plate and the secondary ossification center, but not as many on the articular surface, were H2B-EGFPhigh (Figure 2d, cells with green nuclei).
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 2d.

claim: The short protocol of tamoxifen injection marked a great number of chondrocytes in the growth plate, but a much fewer number of cells in the articular cartilage.
source: This short protocol of tamoxifen injection marked a great number of chondrocytes in the growth plate, but a much fewer number of cells in the articular cartilage (Figure 2d), indicating that this double-color strategy can effectively identify H2B-EGFPhighgrowth plate chondrocytes at this stage.
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 2d.

claim: After 4 weeks of chase, LRCs were identified at a specific location near the top of the growth plate in the resting zone, retaining a higher level of H2B-EGFP signal.
source: Second, Col2-Q mice were fed with doxycycline from P21 to shut off new H2B-EGFP synthesis for 4 weeks (chase) and were then treated with the short protocol of tamoxifen injection After the chase, LRCs were identified at a specific location near the top of the growth plate in the resting zone, retaining a higher level of H2B-EGFP signal (Figure 2e, left panel).
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 2e.

claim: Most H2B-EGFPhigh cells in the growth plate were simultaneously marked as Col2CE-tdT+ after 4 weeks of chase.
source: In addition, most of these H2B-EGFPhigh cells in the growth plate were simultaneously marked as Col2CE-tdT+ (Figure 2e, right panel, arrowhead).
evidence: This is based on observations from Figure 2e.

claim: Chondrocytes with the brightest H2B-GFP signal were localized to the resting zone, and their descendants showed increasingly diluted H2B-EGFP signals as they progressed toward the proliferating and pre-hypertrophic zones.
source: While chondrocytes with the brightest H2B-GFP signal were localized to the resting zone, their descendants showed increasingly diluted H2B-EGFP signals as they progressed toward the proliferating and pre-hypertrophic zones (Figure 1b, Figure 2e, right panel).
evidence: This is based on observations from Figures 1b and 2e.

claim: The Col2-Q quadruple transgenic strategy can effectively mark LRCs primarily in the resting zone of the postnatal growth plate.
source: Therefore, our Col2-Q quadruple transgenic strategy can effectively mark LRCs primarily in the resting zone of the postnatal growth plate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: There were significantly fewer Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes in the articular surface compared to those in the growth plate at P49.
source: Importantly, we observed a significantly fewer number of Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes in the articular surface compared to those in the growth plate at P49 (Figure 3a,b, ; Figure 3—source data 1; GP=1,315.0±171.2 cells; AC=79.1±50.3 cells, n=nine mice [p<0.0001]), consistent with the previous finding that Col2a1-creER preferentially marks growth plate chondrocytes in adulthood (Nagao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data shown in Figure 3a,b with statistical significance.

claim: Col2a1-creER preferentially marks growth plate chondrocytes in adulthood.
source: Importantly, we observed a significantly fewer number of Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes in the articular surface compared to those in the growth plate at P49 (Figure 3a,b, ; Figure 3—source data 1; GP=1,315.0±171.2 cells; AC=79.1±50.3 cells, n=nine mice [p<0.0001]), consistent with the previous finding that Col2a1-creER preferentially marks growth plate chondrocytes in adulthood (Nagao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nagao et al., 2016.

claim: There was a significant reduction in Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes in the growth plate after collagenase digestion.
source: We found a significant reduction in Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes in the growth plate after collagenase digestion (Before: GP=1,315.0±171.2, After: GP=49.8±45.2, n=9 [before], n=4 [after] mice [p=0.003]).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data with statistical significance.

claim: There was no change in the number of Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes in the articular cartilage following collagenase digestion.
source: In contrast, there was no change in the number of Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes in the articular cartilage following collagenase digestion (Before: AC=79.1±50.3, After: AC=85.8±45.2, n=9 [before], n=four mice [after] [p=0.939]).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data with statistical significance.

claim: Growth plate chondrocytes account for 99.1 ± 1.4% of Col2a1CE-tdT+ cells dissociated from the dissected epiphyses.
source: In fact, growth plate chondrocytes account for essentially all of Col2a1CE-tdT+ cells (99.1 ± 1.4% of Col2a1CE-tdT+ cells, n=four mice).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data.

claim: The microdissection and enzymatic dissociation approach allows selective harvest of Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes from the postnatal growth plate.
source: Therefore, these data demonstrate that our microdissection and enzymatic dissociation approach allows us to selectively harvest Col2a1CE-tdT+ chondrocytes from the postnatal growth plate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Col2a1CE-tdT+ cells were clearly distinguishable from unlabeled cells at all time points investigated in CD45-negative non-hematopoietic fraction.
source: Subsequently, we used a flow cytometry-based approach to analyze single cells dissociated from the Col2-Q postnatal growth plate at sequential time points before and after the chase, particularly in a CD45-negative non-hematopoietic fraction. Col2a1CE-tdT+ cells were clearly distinguishable from unlabeled cells at all time points investigated (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Before the chase started at P21, 86.4 ± 5.0% of Col2a1CE-tdT+ cells retained >104 units of H2B-EGFP.
source: Before the chase started at P21 (therefore without doxycycline feeding), 86.4 ± 5.0% of Col2a1CE-tdT+ cells retained >104 units of H2B-EGFP (Figure 4a, leftmost panel).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The fraction of a label-retaining population (GFPhigh, retaining >104 unit of H2B-EGFP signal) within a Col2CE-tdT+ population gradually decreased as the chase period extended.
source: The fraction of a label-retaining population (GFPhigh, retaining >104 unit of H2B-EGFP signal) within a Col2CE-tdT+ population gradually decreased as the chase period extended (Figure 4a,b).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry data shown in Figures 4a and 4b.

claim: The decay of GFPhigh cells fits into a non-linear decay curve with Y0: 86.5 ± 1.3%; Plateau: 2.6 ± 0.9%; T1/2=0.99~1.18 week.
source: These plots fit into a non-linear decay curve (Y0: 86.5 ± 1.3%; Plateau: 2.6 ± 0.9%; T1/2=0.99~1.18 week) (Figure 4c, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on curve fitting of the flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Virtually no GFP+ cells were observed in the absence of a Col2a1-tTA transgene.
source: Virtually no GFP+ cells were observed in the absence of a Col2a1-tTA transgene (Figure 4b, magenta line), while levels of GFP+ cells were maintained from five to ten weeks of chase (Figure 4b, orange and teal lines).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: LRCs can be effectively identified and isolated from postnatal Col2-Q growth plates by combined microdissection, enzymatic digestion and flow cytometry-based approaches.
source: Therefore, these findings demonstrate that LRCs can be effectively identified and isolated from postnatal Col2-Q growth plates by combined microdissection, enzymatic digestion and flow cytometry-based approaches.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Non-LRCs were significantly enriched for EdU+ cells at 1 week and 2 weeks of chase.
source: Non-LRCs were significantly enriched for EdU+ cells, both at 1 week and 2 weeks of chase (EdU+ cells, 1 week: 2.04 ± 1.67% of LRCs; 7.04 ± 2.30% of non-LRCs, n=six mice [p=0.002]; 2 weeks: 1.13 ± 0.74% of LRCs; 2.80 ± 1.00% of non-LRCs, n=eight mice [p=0.047]) (Figure 4d,e left and middle, Figure 4—figure supplement 1a, ; Figure 4—source data 2e).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry data with statistical significance.

claim: There was a trend that non-LRCs were enriched for EdU+ cells at 4 weeks of chase, although not statistically significant.
source: We also found a trend that non-LRCs were enriched for EdU+ cells at 4 weeks of chase, although not statistically significant (EdU+ cells, 2.40 ± 0.85% of LRCs; 4.34 ± 1.89% of non-LRCs, n=four mice [p=0.200] (Figure 4e, right, Figure 4—figure supplement 1b, Figure 4—source data 2e)).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry data without statistical significance.

claim: LRCs are relatively resistant to EdU incorporation, denoting their relatively quiescent status.
source: Therefore, LRCs are relatively resistant to EdU incorporation, denoting their relatively quiescent status.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EdU incorporation data.

claim: Cellular RNA levels from LRCs and non-LRCs had sufficient quality for downstream application (RIN>8.0).
source: To assess RNA quality, we conducted an RNA Integrity Number (RIN) assay (Schroeder et al., 2006) from total RNAs isolated from LRCs and non-LRCs. Cellular RNA levels from each population had sufficient quality for downstream application (RIN>8.0), which were further subjected to amplification and deep sequencing.
evidence: This is based on RNA quality assessment data.

claim: An unsupervised clustering analysis demonstrated that LRCs and non-LRCs biological triplicate samples each clustered together.
source: An unsupervised clustering analysis demonstrated that LRCs and non-LRCs biological triplicate samples each clustered together (Figure 5a), indicating that slow-cycling chondrocytes in the postnatal growth plate possess a biologically unique pattern of transcriptomes compared to more rapidly diving non-LRCs.
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Slow-cycling chondrocytes in the postnatal growth plate possess a biologically unique pattern of transcriptomes compared to more rapidly dividing non-LRCs.
source: An unsupervised clustering analysis demonstrated that LRCs and non-LRCs biological triplicate samples each clustered together (Figure 5a), indicating that slow-cycling chondrocytes in the postnatal growth plate possess a biologically unique pattern of transcriptomes compared to more rapidly diving non-LRCs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the clustering analysis.

claim: 799 genes were differentially expressed between LRCs and non-LRCs (fold change ≥ ± 2), of which 427 and 372 genes were upregulated in LRCs and non-LRCs, respectively.
source: Analyses of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) revealed that 799 genes were differentially expressed between the two groups (fold change ≥ ± 2), of which 427 and 372 genes were upregulated in LRCs and non-LRCs, respectively (Figure 5b, Supplementary File 1).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Representative genes upregulated in LRCs included Pthlh (x2.6), Sfrp5 (x2.4), Gas1 (x12), Spon1 (x10), and Wif1 (x3.8).
source: Representative genes upregulated in LRCs included known markers for resting chondrocytes, such as Pthlh (also known as Pthrp, x2.6) (Chen et al., 2006) and Sfrp5 (x2.4); (Chau et al., 2014; Lui et al., 2010) in addition to novel markers, such as Gas1 (x12), Spon1 (x10), and Wif1 (x3.8).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis with citations for known markers.

claim: Representative genes upregulated in non-LRCs included Ihh (x54), Col10a1 (x11), Mef2c (x5.1), Pth1r (x3.0), Sp7 (x2.4), Dlx5 (x2.2), Clec11a (x2.9), and Cd200 (x2.1).
source: Similarly, representative genes upregulated in non-LRCs included both known and novel markers for proliferating and pre-hypertrophic chondrocytes, such as Ihh (St-Jacques et al., 1999) (x54), Col10a1 (Gu et al., 2014) (x11), Mef2c (Arnold et al., 2007) (x5.1), Pth1r (Hirai et al., 2011) (x3.0), Sp7 (Nakashima et al., 2002) (x2.4), and Dlx5 (Robledo et al., 2002) (x2.2) as well as Clec11a (Yue et al., 2016) (x2.9) and Cd200 (Etich et al., 2015) (x2.1).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis with citations for known markers.

claim: A number of genes encoding S and G2/M phase cell cycle regulators were significantly enriched in non-LRCs, highlighting the mitotically active nature of non-LRCs.
source: Moreover, a number of genes encoding S and G2/M phase cell cycle regsulators were significantly enriched in non-LRCs, highlighting the mitotically active nature of non-LRCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1a,b.

claim: The most highly upregulated gene in LRCs was Prg4, which is a marker for chondrocytes in the superficial layer of the articular surface.
source: We further set out to validate the LRC markers using several independent approaches. Interestingly, the most highly upregulated gene in LRCs was Prg4, which is a marker for chondrocytes in the superficial layer of the articular surface (Lui et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis with a citation.

claim: Prg4 mRNA was detected in the resting zone at P21 and 7 weeks, at a level far fainter than that of the articular surface.
source: At P21, Prg4 mRNA was indeed found in the resting zone, at a level far fainter than that of the articular surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 2a). By 7 weeks, Prg4 mRNA was also detected in the resting zone in a similar pattern (Figure 5c, arrows, Figure 5—figure supplement 2b, arrows).
evidence: This is based on RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figures 5c and 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Gas1+ cells were exclusively found at the top of the growth plate corresponding to the resting zone at P14.
source: Second, we validated expression of a novel LRC marker, Gas1. Analysis of Gas1-LacZ knock-in mice (Martinelli and Fan, 2007) at P14 revealed that Gas1+ cells were exclusively found at the top of the growth plate corresponding to the resting zone (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is based on analysis of Gas1-LacZ reporter mice shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Shortly after EdU pulse at P7, 17.9 ± 2.7% of EdU+ cells were PTHrP+ in PthlhLacZ knock-in mice.
source: Shortly after the pulse at P7, PTHrP+ cells were preferentially localized in an EdU-low zone, wherein 17.9 ± 2.7% of EdU+ cells were PTHrP+ (Figure 5e, left panel, and Figure 5f).
evidence: This is based on EdU pulse-chase data shown in Figures 5e and 5f.

claim: After 22 days of chase at P28, 77.6 ± 9.6% of EdU+ cells were PTHrP+ in PthlhLacZ knock-in mice.
source: After 22 days of chase at P28, a great majority of EdU-retaining cells were PTHrP+, wherein 77.6 ± 9.6% of EdU+ cells were PTHrP+ (Figure 5e, right panel, and Figure 5f, ; Figure 5—source data 1f).
evidence: This is based on EdU pulse-chase data shown in Figures 5e and 5f.

claim: LRCs become increasingly enriched among PTHrP+ chondrocytes in the postnatal growth plate.
source: Therefore, LRCs become increasingly enriched among PTHrP+ chondrocytes in the postnatal growth plate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EdU pulse-chase data in PthlhLacZ mice.

claim: Pathway analysis of DEGs revealed significant enrichment of four KEGG terms (p<0.05, FDR), including Oxidative phosphorylation, Wnt signaling pathway, Endocrine and other factor-regulated calcium reabsorption, and Pathways in cancer.
source: Pathway analysis of DEGs revealed significant enrichment of four KEGG terms (p<0.05, FDR), including Oxidative phosphorylation (KEGG:00190), Wnt signaling pathway (KEGG:04310), Endocrine and other factor-regulated calcium reabsorption (KEGG:04961) and Pathways in cancer (KEGG:05200) (Figure 5g).
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis shown in Figure 5g.

claim: All DEGs annotated under the Oxidative phosphorylation KEGG term were upregulated in non-LRCs, highlighting a biochemically unique feature of non-LRCs undergoing active processes such as cell division and differentiation.
source: Notably, all DEGs annotated under the Oxidative phosphorylation KEGG term were upregulated in non-LRCs, highlighting a biochemically unique feature of non-LRCs undergoing active processes such as cell division and differentiation.
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis with an interpretation of the biological significance.

claim: Out of 21 DEGs annotated in Wnt signaling pathway, 16 genes were relevant to the canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathways.
source: Out of 21 DEGs annotated in Wnt signaling pathway, 16 genes were relevant to the canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathways (Komiya and Habas, 2008; Figure 5h).
evidence: This is based on pathway analysis shown in Figure 5h with a citation.

claim: LRCs were enriched for genes encoding Wnt inhibitors such as Sfrp1, Sfrp5, Dkk2, Wif1, Notum and Fzd6, the Wnt activator Wnt7b, and Wnt receptors Fzd1, Fzd3 and Fzd8.
source: LRCs were enriched for genes encoding Wnt inhibitors such as Sfrp1, Sfrp5, Dkk2, Wif1, Notum and Fzd6, the Wnt activator, Wnt7b, and Wnt receptors Fzd1, Fzd3 and Fzd8.
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Non-LRCs were enriched for genes encoding Wnt activators such as Rspo3, Rspo4 and Wnt10b.
source: Conversely, non-LRCs were enriched for genes encoding Wnt activators such as Rspo3, Rspo4 and Wnt10b (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5h.

claim: LRCs reside in a microenvironment in which inhibitors for canonical Wnt signaling are abundantly present in the milieu.
source: Therefore, these RNA-seq analyses demonstrate that LRCs reside in a microenvironment in which inhibitors for canonical Wnt signaling are abundantly present in the milieu (Figure 5i).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNA-seq data.

claim: Apc haploinsufficiency significantly upregulated β-catenin protein in the resting zone of APC cHet growth plates.
source: Immunohistochemical analysis revealed that the β-catenin protein was significantly upregulated in the resting zone of APC cHet growth plates (CTNNB-Alexa 647 signal: Control, 62.1±33.3; APC cHet: 283.9±65.8, n=four mice [p=0.03]), as well as in PTHrPCEtdTomato+ cells therein (Figure 6d, leftmost panels, arrows, quantification shown in Figure 6e, Figure 6—source data 1e-h), indicating that Apc haploinsufficiency indeed slows β-catenin degradation and activated canonical Wnt signaling specifically in the resting zone of the growth plate.
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 6d with statistical significance.

claim: Apc haploinsufficiency slows β-catenin degradation and activated canonical Wnt signaling specifically in the resting zone of the growth plate.
source: Immunohistochemical analysis revealed that the β-catenin protein was significantly upregulated in the resting zone of APC cHet growth plates (CTNNB-Alexa 647 signal: Control, 62.1±33.3; APC cHet: 283.9±65.8, n=four mice [p=0.03]), as well as in PTHrPCEtdTomato+ cells therein (Figure 6d, leftmost panels, arrows, quantification shown in Figure 6e, Figure 6—source data 1e-h), indicating that Apc haploinsufficiency indeed slows β-catenin degradation and activated canonical Wnt signaling specifically in the resting zone of the growth plate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the β-catenin upregulation data.

claim: PTHrPCEAPCHet resting chondrocytes did not increase in number during the initial stage of chase, and the numbers were significantly lower than those of Control at P9, P12, and P21.
source: In contrast, PTHrPCEAPCHet resting chondrocytes did not increase in number during the initial stage of chase, the numbers of which were significantly lower than those of Control at the initial three time points (P9: 474.8±134.8 [p=0.04], P12: 558.4±64.3 [p=0.03], P21: 443.4±79.2 [p=0.03] cells, Figure 6f, red line, n=4–5 mice), and fell to levels that were similar to those in the Control at the latter two time points (Figure 6d, rightmost panel, and Figure 6f).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data shown in Figure 6f with statistical significance.

claim: The formation and the expansion of PTHrP+ cells in the resting zone are slightly impaired when canonical Wnt signaling is activated in these cells.
source: These data indicate that the formation and the expansion of PTHrP+ cells in the resting zone are slightly impaired when canonical Wnt signaling is activated in these cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantitative data on resting chondrocytes.

claim: The number of tdTomato+ short columns in APC cHet growth plates was reduced at P21.
source: The number of tdTomato+ short columns in APC cHet growth plates was reduced at P21 (P21: 45.9±7.7 tdTomato+ columns, Figure 6g, red line, n=four mice [p=0.03]), indicating that the formation of short columnar chondrocytes in the proliferating zone is inhibited upon canonical Wnt signaling activation.
evidence: This is based on quantitative data shown in Figure 6g with statistical significance.

claim: The formation of short columnar chondrocytes in the proliferating zone is inhibited upon canonical Wnt signaling activation.
source: The number of tdTomato+ short columns in APC cHet growth plates was reduced at P21 (P21: 45.9±7.7 tdTomato+ columns, Figure 6g, red line, n=four mice [p=0.03]), indicating that the formation of short columnar chondrocytes in the proliferating zone is inhibited upon canonical Wnt signaling activation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the quantitative data on short columns.

claim: The number of tdTomato+ long columns in APC cHet growth plates was significantly decreased at P96.
source: In contrast, the number of tdTomato+ long columns in APC cHet growth plates was significantly decreased at P96 (P96: 7.3±2.5 tdTomato+ columns, Figure 6h, red line, n=four mice [p=0.03]).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data shown in Figure 6h with statistical significance.

claim: The ability for PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes to clonally establish columnar chondrocytes is slightly impaired in response to activation of canonical Wnt signaling in the resting zone.
source: Therefore, the ability for PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes to clonally establish columnar chondrocytes is slightly impaired in response to activation of canonical Wnt signaling in the resting zone.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantitative data on long columns.

claim: Activation of canonical Wnt signaling impairs formation, expansion and differentiation of PTHrP+ chondrocytes in the resting zone.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that activation of canonical Wnt signaling impairs formation, expansion and differentiation of PTHrP+ chondrocytes in the resting zone (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the Apc haploinsufficiency experiments.

claim: PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes are required to be maintained in a Wnt-inhibitory environment to maintain themselves and their column-forming capabilities.
source: Thus, PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes are required to be maintained in a Wnt-inhibitory environment to maintain themselves and their column-forming capabilities.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on all the experimental data.

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling is essential for endochondral ossification.
source: Wnt/β-catenin signaling is essential for endochondral ossification (Regard et al., 2012), and is shown to regulate initiation of chondrocyte hypertrophy by inhibiting PTHrP signaling activities (Guo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Regard et al., 2012 and Guo et al., 2009.

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling regulates initiation of chondrocyte hypertrophy by inhibiting PTHrP signaling activities.
source: Wnt/β-catenin signaling is essential for endochondral ossification (Regard et al., 2012), and is shown to regulate initiation of chondrocyte hypertrophy by inhibiting PTHrP signaling activities (Guo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Guo et al., 2009.

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling is essential during skeletal development for regulating mesenchymal progenitor differentiation in favor of osteoblasts.
source: Moreover, Wnt/β-catenin signaling is essential during skeletal development for regulating mesenchymal progenitor differentiation in favor of osteoblasts (Day et al., 2005), or for preventing transdifferentiation of osteoblast precursors into chondrocytes (Hill et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Day et al., 2005 and Hill et al., 2005.

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling is essential for preventing transdifferentiation of osteoblast precursors into chondrocytes.
source: Moreover, Wnt/β-catenin signaling is essential during skeletal development for regulating mesenchymal progenitor differentiation in favor of osteoblasts (Day et al., 2005), or for preventing transdifferentiation of osteoblast precursors into chondrocytes (Hill et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hill et al., 2005.

claim: The effect of β-catenin stabilization in PTHrP+ chondrocytes appears to be modest.
source: It is important to note that the effect of β-catenin stabilization in PTHrP+ chondrocytes appears to be modest.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Non-canonical Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling plays a key role in facilitating asymmetric divisions of resting chondrocytes.
source: Lines of studies demonstrate that non-canonical Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling plays a key role in facilitating asymmetric divisions of resting chondrocytes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: Canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling pathways concertedly modulate PTHrP+ chondrocytes in the resting zone and regulate their differentiation.
source: Therefore, our findings support the notion that canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling pathways concertedly modulate PTHrP+ chondrocytes in the resting zone and regulate their differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and existing knowledge.
